pr_title: dma: callback to allow for positive statuses on success
pr_body:
Make use of positive status values in the DMA callback to pass info to the DMA client after a successful DMA operation. The status integer is dependent to the DMA implementation and might differ on each platform.

Fixes #52417

cc @teburd

issue_context.title: RFC: API Change: dma: callback status
issue_context.body:
## Introduction

Provide contextual information in the DMA callback.

### Problem description

DMA API allows for one callback, with one success status (`0`), even though there might be more than one DMA event/interrupt.

### Proposed change

The current callback can be leveraged without modifying its signature to pass more information into the `status` parameter:
```c
typedef void (*dma_callback_t)(const struct device *dev, void *user_data,
			       uint32_t channel, int status);
```

## Detailed RFC

The DMA driver has the ability to configure one callback called whenever a DMA transfer is completed. Below is the current description for this callback which is set when configuring the DMA device (see `struct dma_config`):

```c
/**
 * @typedef dma_callback_t
 * @brief Callback function for DMA transfer completion
 *
 *  If enabled, callback function will be invoked at transfer completion
 *  or when error happens.
 *
 * @param dev Pointer to the DMA device calling the callback.
 * @param user_data A pointer to some user data or NULL
 * @param channel The channel number
 * @param status 0 on success, a negative errno otherwise
 */
typedef void (*dma_callback_t)(const struct device *dev, void *user_data,
			       uint32_t channel, int status);
```

Usage of DMA on different microcontrollers might differ. For example, most STM32 microcontrollers have two interrupts: one for half complete, and one for fully complete transfer. It might be needed to call the DMA callback for both of these interrupts and the user of the DMA device might need to be informed about which interrupt occurred. It is not possible at this point to pass this kind of information using the current API description: 0 on success meaning when DMA transfer completes.

The `dma_get_status()` function could be used to _guess_ which interrupt occurred but the current status of DMA might have changed by the time the user calls the `dma_get_status()` function (it happened to me when working on https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/51795) and we might want to process the buffers differently depending on the source of the interrupt, not the current status.

### Proposed change (Detailed)

Change the `dma_callback_t` description so that any positive `status` gives information about the source of the interrupt, which might differ depending on the platform: STM32 might use 2 status codes for fully and half complete while other platforms might use only 1 status code.

Pull Request #52780

This is the new documentation for the callback:

```c
/**
 * @typedef dma_callback_t
 * @brief Callback function for DMA transfer completion
 *
 *  If enabled, callback function will be invoked at transfer completion
 *  or when error happens.
 *
 * @param dev Pointer to the DMA device calling the callback.
 * @param user_data A pointer to some user data or NULL
 * @param channel The channel number
 * @param status 0 or positive value on success, a negative errno otherwise
 */
typedef void (*dma_callback_t)(const struct device *dev, void *user_data,
			       uint32_t channel, int status);
```

### Dependencies

Several Zephyr drivers are using the DMA API (I2S, UART, SPI) as well as some tests and it is also possible that Zephyr users use the DMA driver directly in their source code.

The one change needed by these users is to modify their callback implementation to account for the status value that can only be negative on error, from this:
```c
if (status != 0) { error_path(); }
```
to this:
```
if (status < 0) { error_path(); }
```

## Alternatives

Store several callbacks, one for each interrupt sources in the platform-dependent implementation, like done in `dma_dw_common.h`:

```c
struct dw_dma_chan_data {
        // ...
	dma_callback_t dma_blkcallback; // block complete callback
	void *blkuser_data;
	dma_callback_t dma_tfrcallback; // transfer complete callback 
	void *tfruser_data;
}
```

I don't think this is a bad idea and actually stumbled upon this implementation while writing this issue. It has the advantage of having one user data pointer per callback instead of one for all the interrupt sources.

Let me know if you have preferences.
comments: Also worth mentioning #37372 which proposes to use an enum to give the status, which would be shared across all the DMA implementations

I dived a bit more into it and the `dma.h` `struct dma_config` only has one callback used when configuring a DMA device so I don't think it's that easy to store several callbacks. It would involve calling the `.config` function of `struct dma_driver_api` several times with parameters to configure the DMA clients with the different callbacks...

I think the idea of having a negative status for errors and any positive value for status about a DMA interrupt is the best option.

cc @teburd let me know what you think, I can submit a PR to change the DMA API description and status handling (make sure `status < 0` for errors instead of `status != 0`.

I'd say send a PR, I'm ok with updating the status to indicate more information than error or success.

For the circular modes this makes good sense. This change will require some careful review though of the code base to ensure status != 0 isn't being used to check for the error case. While not exactly breaking the API (0 is still success), it is changing expectations of how the API works. So in that regard we may need to ensure broadcast this change in a few places. I need to review the projects requirements around stable API changes and if this would constitute one.

I'll repeat that I'm ok changing the status given to the callback. That said it does seem like we'll need to go through the stable API change procedure to change it if that's the approach you'd like to take.

Please change the issue title to one similar to the stable API change RFC title noted here, https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/api/api_lifecycle.html#introducing-incompatible-changes and make sure all the fields are here (I believe they are).

Alternatively you could try the approach taken by dw dma as you noted with multiple callback pointers (one for each possible interrupt trigger event) which could possibly done without changing the stable API.
Thanks @erwango, I was out for the holidays
@teburd any chance to see this discussed during the weekly meeting?
Architecture WG: Some agreement, some request for more design on possible use cases beyond this STM32 part's half-full/full behavior.

For the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/51795 is a change in the status really needed?  If I'm understanding the code change there is more about if the callback is a cyclic callback or not.  Can't that be determined in the callback in the uart based on how `cyclic` got configured?

I also had a similar problem when implementing a DMA-based ADC driver. I manually checked the DMA channel's current destination address to determine the buffer position.

Some DMA peripherals, like the one in the NXP K64 family, support the automatic loading of a different transfer configuration at the end of the current transfer on the same channel (commonly known as the scatter-gather feature). The current DMA callback does not also have a way to tell which DMA transfer generated the interrupt.

Adding the destination address and the number of bytes transferred to the callback would be a more generic approach.
This approach would provide the necessary information for the API user regarding interrupts of both half-fill/full and automatic transfer configuration loading cases.
We should make the return code well defined.  So 0 means DMA complete, and 1 means circular water mark complete.
